tetris-introduction: Tetris is a classic arcade game where the goal is to stack falling geometric pieces to form complete horizontal lines and score points.
tetris-description:
The development of the Tetris project using Swing in Java allowed the practical application of object-oriented programming concepts for the first time.

This project was also an opportunity to strengthen skills in managing properties files to offer multilingual options, as well as in integrating music to enhance the user experience.

This experience led to an in-depth understanding of architecture and programming techniques, preparing for similar challenges in the future and improving software development skills.
azul-introduction: Azul is a strategic game for 2 to 4 players who decorate a Portuguese palace with colorful tiles. The goal is to score points by creating patterns on a personal board, choosing and placing tiles wisely to maximize scores and minimize penalties.
azul-description:
The MVC (Model, View, Controller) architecture was adopted to simplify the distribution of responsibilities and ensure a robust, easily modifiable program for future adaptations. To optimize productivity and provide clear benchmarks, several UML diagrams were developed to determine the project's requirements and needs. Then, various class diagrams were designed to establish the ideal architecture before starting the coding phase.

This project represented a valuable opportunity to strengthen skills in software architecture, enriching knowledge of development beyond simple programming.
twitturtle-introduction:
A pun between Twitter and Turtle: Website derived from the famous social network, specialized for pet owners with additional features, such as:

➜ The ability to add a pet to your profile
➜ Tag animals in a post, add a location, and a type of post (event, advice, rescue)
➜ Adopt an animal through a request and notification system
➜ And many more features
twitturtle-description:
This project was an exceptional opportunity for skill development in various fields. It allowed the initiation into JavaScript and the exploration of different APIs, notably those offered by Google Cloud.

Additionally, new skills were acquired by sending emails using the PHPMailer library and using the services of the company Sendinblue.
pogo-introduction:
Pogo is a strategy game for two players, suitable for children aged 6 and up. It is easy to learn (about 2 minutes) and quick to play (about 10 minutes). The game includes a nine-square board and twelve stackable pieces (six light and six dark). The goal is to be the first player to place a piece of their color at the top of each stack on the board.

In this computer-adapted game, an AI can fight against a user or against itself.
pogo-description:
A major challenge of this project was designing an evaluation method to determine the best move for the AI. This evaluation integrated various factors, such as the position of the tower, the number of tokens in its possession, the ability to capture an opponent's tower or protect itself from capture, as well as the possible movement distance.

This project strengthened skills in Python and understanding the implementation of the MinMax algorithm. Additionally, skills in creating graphical interfaces were developed using the QT library.
unity-introduction:
Small project realized on Unity, which includes 3 different mini-games:

➜ Apple Catcher
➜ Brick Breaker
➜ Furapi Bird
unity-description: This project offered the opportunity to discover the workings of Unity and explore new possibilities in game design. It also allowed initiation into the C# programming language. Being very close to Java, this language facilitated adaptation and leveraging the skills acquired during the project.
ludiq-introduction: Ludiq is a platform dedicated to sharing hobbies and activities through a website. Users can create discussions, publish posts, organize activities, and events related to their interests. These events are open to members who share the same passions.
ludiq-description:
The project was developed with a Backend architecture in PHP and a Front-end in Angular. To ensure a robust structure, a Model - Services - Controller architecture was implemented.

This project provided the opportunity to become familiar with a framework and to master the concept of components, thereby enabling the development of more flexible and sustainable websites.
patrolling-introduction: This project aims to simulate the movements of several agents patrolling in a virtual museum, whose configuration can be freely defined. The main idea is to analyze and optimize the patrol routes in order to find the most efficient paths, depending on parameters such as the number of agents and the structure of the museum.
patrolling-description: In carrying out this project, we studied and compared different algorithms such as K-Means, Ant Colony Optimization, and Genetic Algorithms, in order to identify the most effective movement strategies. The graphical interface was developed with Pygame-CE, and Numpy was used for the implementation of the algorithms. The project was structured following an MVC architecture to clearly separate models from views. A continuous integration pipeline was also set up with SonarCloud to ensure code quality, while unit tests with pytest and tox validated the reliability of the program.
blender-introduction: The purpose of this project was to create a 3D scene in Blender while applying various modeling and visual design techniques.
blender-description: The work was carried out both during practical lab sessions and outside of class. The goal was to design a cozy and visually appealing scene, making use of different Blender tools and methods such as modifiers, UV mapping, as well as various texturing and lighting techniques.
portfolio-introduction: This portfolio is designed to showcase my projects, skills, and background as a computer engineer.
portfolio-description: The creation of this portfolio, which you are currently viewing, allowed me to put into practice my knowledge of web development, focusing on design and usability. I used Figma to design a pleasant and tailored user interface. The development is based on React, whose robust structure (built on services and reusable components) enables me to efficiently update and evolve this portfolio over time.
fracture-introduction: Fracture is an interactive Discord application where multiple players coordinate their actions around a crystal. The goal is to earn points by absorbing the crystal's power while preventing it from breaking, which would make all participants lose their session points. The game emphasizes strategic choices inspired by the prisoner's dilemma: cooperate to maximize collective gains, or try to get an advantage over others at the risk of losing everything.
fracture-description: The project is built on a full-stack architecture with a Node.js backend using Express and Mongoose to interact with MongoDB, enabling management of players, bonuses, and sessions. The frontend is developed in React with TailwindCSS. The application uses sockets to synchronize players' actions in real time. The system follows a robust architecture with reusable services, facilitating maintenance and long-term evolution of the application.
vocaboost-introduction: Vocaboost is a mobile application that I created (still in progress) to further develop my skills in mobile development and explore the Android ecosystem. The app helps me review specific german vocabulary that I import myself. The goal is to have a simple and efficient tool to learn, with progress tracking and an intelligent review system.
vocaboost-description:
The project is based on a complete full-stack architecture:

 ➜ The backend is developed in Java with Spring Boot. It manages the business logic, database queries to PostgreSQL (thanks to Hibernate and JPARepository), and data persistence (words, progress, history, statistics, etc.).
 ➜ The frontend is an Android application built with Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Material 3, offering a modern and responsive interface based on composables.
 ➜ Google Sign-In is also implemented through Google Cloud and Firebase Authentication, allowing users to log in easily and securely without handling passwords manually.

Vocaboost allows me to combine mobile and backend development while working on aspects like data persistence, authentication, and ergonomic interface design.

ut_rc-description: UT RC is a club at UTBM dedicated to enthusiasts of remote-controlled vehicles and devices via radio signals, such as cars, drones, etc.

eventum-description: Eventum is a website created as part of a UTBM project to bring students together for outings, evenings, and other events.
axopen-info: I had the opportunity to work at Axopen as part of my assistant engineer internship during my fourth year of studies. Axopen is a company specialized in web development and audits. This internships allowed me to develop my skills in web development and immerse myself in a professional environment while collaborating within a team.
axopen-project-one: This project involved setting up a portal for a client to facilitate the verification of EXCEL files sent by country representatives. This project allowed me to improve my teamwork skills and gain more experience with frameworks such as Laravel (which uses PHP as programming language) for back-end development and React for front-end development.
axopen-project-two: This was a project aimed at creating a program that generates SVG diagrams representing the architecture between applications, hosting services, and explains their operation through processes or connections. This project allowed me to develop my skills in C# programming language as well as the .NET framework. It also introduced me to GitLab, a development and hosting platform based on Git.
bosch-info: I had the great opportunity to work at Bosch, a global leader in technology and engineering, where I participated in the development and automation of applications for the department. This experience allowed me to strengthen my skills in international communication, work effectively in a team, and collaborate across different departments, while applying and deepening my technical knowledge in a professional context.
bosch-project-one: I developed a CRON job to automatically transfer files every night from an SMB fileshare to a dedicated SharePoint, making the data accessible to an external application, which was also the application where I performed End-to-End (E2E) tests with Cypress. These tests ensured that the application continued to function correctly after the addition of new features. The automation required simulating a user login, which led me to understand and use OAuth2 to interact properly with the application.
bosch-project-two: During this project, I automated the renaming of files on SharePoint using Power Automate, in order to follow a precise convention and ensure effective tracking of departmental files through a list serving as a database. I also developed a user interface with Power Apps to facilitate targeted file searches. Finally, I designed and distributed an internal newsletter, allowing each department member to contribute and easily share relevant content.
bosch-project-one-title: First Project - File Transfer Automation and E2E Testing
